feat(ErdosProblems): formalize problem 561 (#7124)

Formalize Erdős Problem 561, the size Ramsey formula for two star
forests with nonincreasing positive star sizes.

Use the existing `SimpleGraph.sizeRamsey`. Problem-local notation
constructs the vertex-disjoint stars from a relation on tagged finite
vertex sets; vertex 0 is each component's center. The right-hand side
sums finite maxima over one-based index diagonals. Positive sizes make
natural subtraction safe, and every diagonal is nonempty.

The statement was independently audited against all four pages of the
supplied PDF and https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/561. The current
source uses the summation endpoint `s + t`, correcting the older issue
text's `s + 2`. The general conjecture remains tagged `research open`:
https://arxiv.org/html/2606.04439v3 treats uniform forests and still
states the general formula as Conjecture 1.1. The original
general-solution claim is not used as evidence of a solution.

Validation: `lake --wfail build 'FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«561»'`
(Lean 4.33.1; Mathlib `0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474`).
Separate Lean checks cover center-to-leaf edges, absence of loops,
leaf-to-leaf and cross-component edges, and the one-star diagonal
maximum.

This is a conjecture statement with an intentional `sorry` proof, not a
formal proof. Supplementary solved cases and forum proof claims are
outside this change.

Prepared with Codex using the Erdős Research Lab skills.

Fixes #791.

+-/
+module
+
+public import FormalConjecturesUtil
+
+/-!
+# Erdős Problem 561
+
+*References:*
+- [erdosproblems.com/561](https://www.erdosproblems.com/561)
+- [BEFRS78] Burr, S. A. and Erdős, P. and Faudree, R. J. and Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H.,
+  Ramsey-minimal graphs for multiple copies. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch. Indag. Math. (1978), 187-195.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Erdos561
+
+open SimpleGraph
+
+/-- `F(s,n)` is the disjoint union of the stars $K_{1,n_i}$. The vertex $(i,0)$ is the center
+of component $i$; its other $n_i$ vertices are leaves. -/
+local notation "F(" s ", " n ")" =>
+  fromRel (fun (u v : Σ i : Fin s, Fin (n i + 1)) ↦
+    Sigma.fst u = Sigma.fst v ∧
+      (Fin.val (Sigma.snd u) = 0 ∨ Fin.val (Sigma.snd v) = 0))
+
+/--
+Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there
+is a graph $H$ with $m$ edges such that in any $2$-colouring of the edges of $H$ there is a
+monochromatic copy of $G$.
+
+Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be the union of stars. More precisely, let
+$F_1=\cup_{i\leq s}K_{1,n_i}$ and $F_2=\cup_{j\leq t}K_{1,m_j}$ with
+$n_1\geq\cdots\geq n_s\geq1$ and $m_1\geq\cdots\geq m_t\geq1$. Prove that
+$$\hat{R}(F_1,F_2)=\sum_{2\leq k\leq s+t}l_k$$
+where
+$$l_k=\max\{n_i+m_j-1:i+j=k\}.$$
+
+The unions are vertex-disjoint, and $s,t\geq1$. Lean indices start at zero, so the condition
+$i+j=k$ is represented by $(i+1)+(j+1)=k$.
+-/
+@[category research open, AMS 5]
+theorem erdos_561 :
+    ∀ (s t : ℕ), 1 ≤ s → 1 ≤ t →
+    ∀ (n : Fin s → ℕ) (m : Fin t → ℕ),
+      Antitone n → Antitone m → (∀ i, 1 ≤ n i) → (∀ j, 1 ≤ m j) →
+      sizeRamsey F(s, n) F(t, m) =
+        ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (s + t),
+          ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin s × Fin t)).filter
+            (fun p ↦ (p.1.val + 1) + (p.2.val + 1) = k)).sup
+              (fun p ↦ n p.1 + m p.2 - 1) := by
+  sorry
+
+end Erdos561
